title: Cisco AI Defense Finding Promotion Health
exclusions: Does not list the guardrail events themselves. That is UC-10.3.9.
evidence: Daily event and promoted counts, and days marked not promoting.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Enable Promote AI Defense events to ES findings, send a test prompt that the policy blocks, and confirm a cisco:ai:defense:notable event. The day stays ok.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Turn promotion off while guardrail events continue. The next day is marked not promoting.

dataSources: `index=ai_defense` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) AI Defense input, which receives events over HEC: `sourcetype=cisco:ai:defense` and, when Promote AI Defense events to ES findings is enabled, `sourcetype=cisco:ai:defense:notable`. Guardrail field names are documented by Splunk Security Content for cisco:ai:defense; this search uses only the sourcetype.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), AI Defense input. Splunk Enterprise Security for the findings.
spl:
index=ai_defense (sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense" OR sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense:notable") earliest=-7d@d latest=@h
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count(eval(sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense")) as events count(eval(sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense:notable")) as promoted by _time
| eval status=case(events > 0 AND promoted = 0, "not promoting", true(), "ok")
| sort - _time
description: Compares daily Cisco AI Defense guardrail events with the notable-ready copies written when promotion to Enterprise Security findings is enabled, and marks a day not promoting when events arrived and none were copied.
value: AI Defense blocks prompt injection and data leaks inside the AI Defense console. The SOC only sees them if promotion is copying those events into Enterprise Security. This report shows the days when that copy produced nothing.
implementation: On the AI Defense input, enable Promote AI Defense events to ES findings. Alert when a day has guardrail events and zero notable-ready events.
visualization: Column chart of events and promoted by day. Table of days with status not promoting.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide
Splunk Security Content data source: Cisco AI Defense Alerts

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Quiet applications** — a day with no prompts has events=0 and is ok, not a promotion failure.

**Suppression:** alert only on status=not promoting.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• AI Defense configured to send to this Splunk HEC token. Splunk Enterprise Security if the copies should become findings.
• An index for this data (this page uses `ai_defense`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the AI Defense card, and create an input. Set the index to `ai_defense`.
• The input writes `cisco:ai:defense` for guardrail events and `cisco:ai:defense:notable` when promotion is enabled.
• Confirm events arrive: `index=ai_defense sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense" or sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense:notable" | stats count`.

Step 2 — Create the search
```spl
index=ai_defense (sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense" OR sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense:notable") earliest=-7d@d latest=@h
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count(eval(sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense")) as events count(eval(sourcetype="cisco:ai:defense:notable")) as promoted by _time
| eval status=case(events > 0 AND promoted = 0, "not promoting", true(), "ok")
| sort - _time
```

Understanding this SPL
• Same shape as the XDR promotion check. `events` is the guardrail feed; `promoted` is the notable-ready copy.
• Field names such as event_action and policy.policy_name belong to UC-10.3.9, not this health check.

Step 3 — Validate
• In AI Defense, open the events for one blocked prompt and confirm the same hour has a cisco:ai:defense event. With promotion on, a cisco:ai:defense:notable event should follow.

• Confirm in the vendor console that the same hour shows the same kind of event before trusting a zero or a spike.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Put the panel on the SOC dashboard for AI Defense and refresh it hourly.
• Alert when the count drops to zero during a staffed period, which means the input stopped, and throttle for 4 hours.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• Guardrail events arrive and notable events do not: the promote option is off, or Enterprise Security is not installed. The user guide says findings require Enterprise Security.
• No guardrail events: the HEC token or the AI Defense Splunk integration (Administration > Integrations > Splunk) is wrong.
• No data for this sourcetype, with an input error in the Cisco Security Cloud log, means the credential or token is incorrect.
grandmaExplanation: We check that blocked AI requests are still being copied into the security queue, and we flag days when that copy stopped.
